paragraphs: §1 — Reading according to the written text

"Ismaʿīl al-ʿUkbarī" abolished the "written and the read" (the ketiv and the qere), claiming that the reading must be according to what is written. Another statement is reported of him that contradicts this one — namely that he claimed there are in Scripture things not as they are now written. Such is his saying [Gen 4:8]: "וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל הֶבֶל אָחִיו" — he claimed there was after it "קוּם נֵצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה"; and His saying [Exod 20:18]: "וְכָל הָעָם רֹאִים אֶת הַקֹּלֹת" — he claimed it was "שׁוֹמְעִים אֶת הַקֹּלֹת," since sounds are not seen but heard. We have already said that this belongs to the Samaritans; perhaps he heard it from their statement and took it from them.

He said: His saying [Exod 16:35] "וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָכְלוּ אֶת הַמָּן" is only "יֹאכְלוּ"; for they, at the time of this statement, had not [yet] eaten it forty years, but [Scripture] reported that they would eat it forty years. Likewise His saying [Gen 46:15] "כָּל נֶפֶשׁ בָּנָיו וּבְנוֹתָיו שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשָׁלֹשׁ" — he claimed it was "שְׁלֹשִׁים וּשְׁתַּיִם," and that this is an error of the scribe.

With him: whenever the new moon is born — which is the time of its parting from the sun — that time is the head of the month, and from that time prayer and offering are obligatory, even if it is an hour before sunset. He permitted, on the day of the Sabbath, eating what the "dissenters" prepared on the Sabbath, such as cooked eggplant, fruits picked on the Sabbath, and the like. He has many statements of the utmost corruption, ugliness, and grotesquerie.

With this, he sets out in his books the disparagement of "ʿAnan" and ascribes to him folly and foolishness. We have already reported above what he commanded his adherents to write upon his grave [2 Kgs 2:12]: "רֶכֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל וּפָרָשָׁיו."
: Abolishing the qere/ketiv — a radical Karaite view: Ismaʿīl is presented as requiring reading by the written text alone, without "tradition," a mark of the "pure Karaites" of his time.
: This is the Samaritan addition at Gen 4:8 — a reading that links Ismaʿīl to a Samaritan view and lowers his credibility in Q's eyes.
: Ismaʿīl disparages ʿAnan — though ʿAnan is the father of the "heads of the ʿAnanites" and the source of the ʿAnaniyya; his internal inconsistency, for Q.
